claim: IdentityLookup does not provide CediWise with general inbox scanning or a durable app-owned SMS receiver; it is a restricted unknown-sender filtering extension.
notes: The conclusion follows from the documented API scope and extension restrictions; Apple does not publish one universal statement naming every unavailable inbox API.

claim: Shortcuts supports user-configured automations triggered by incoming messages with sender or text filters, and Message automations can run automatically.
notes: Opening a third-party app from an automation still needs on-device verification, especially while locked.

claim: An encoded Shortcuts handoff can be routed into the Expo app with a custom-scheme URL and read as route query parameters.
notes: Apple documents encoded URL text; Expo documents custom app links and query parameters. The exact Shortcuts action sequence is not an Apple-provided CediWise integration.

claim: Current Shortcuts releases include Messages search actions that may support a user-run historical lookup workflow.
notes: The release notes establish the actions; bulk transfer, supported fields, and limits remain unverified.

claim: The feature should obtain explicit consent and protect message data before passing it to the CediWise import service.
notes: The App Review guideline is a policy source; CediWise copy must also stay aligned with actual backend retention and privacy disclosures.

claim: The current iOS implementation reuses the authenticated CediWise message import path and remains source-level only until device validation.
notes: No iPhone build, Shortcuts automation, or runtime import was executed in this work.
